title: What Is Programmatic Advertising? A Complete Guide

facts.fact: The page states that a full programmatic ad auction, from page load to ad delivery, typically completes in 80 to 120 milliseconds.
facts.quote: This entire process — from page load to ad delivery — typically completes in 80 to 120 milliseconds.

facts.fact: The page gives a single example auction that took about 100 milliseconds to complete.
facts.quote: The whole auction took about 100 milliseconds.

facts.fact: The page states, without citing a source, that programmatic accounts for over 90% of digital display ad spending in the US.
facts.unit: % of US digital display ad spending
facts.quote: programmatic now accounts for over 90% of digital display ad spending in the US.

facts.fact: The page states that programmatic auctions run millions of times per second across the open web.
facts.quote: It runs millions of times per second across the open web.

facts.fact: The page states that a programmatic campaign can run across millions of publishers simultaneously with the same campaign settings.
facts.quote: Programmatic buys mean your ads run across millions of publishers simultaneously

facts.fact: The page names Google's AdX, Microsoft's Xandr, and Magnite's marketplace as major ad exchanges.
facts.quote: Major exchanges include Google's AdX, Microsoft's Xandr, and Magnite's marketplace.

facts.fact: The page names The Trade Desk, DV360, Xandr, and StackAdapt as major demand-side platforms (DSPs).
facts.quote: The Trade Desk, DV360 (Google's DSP), Xandr, and StackAdapt are major DSPs.

facts.fact: The page states that there are dozens of DSPs in addition to the major ones it names.
The page names Magnite, OpenX, and PubMatic as major supply-side platforms (SSPs).
facts.quote: Major SSPs include Magnite, OpenX, and PubMatic.

facts.fact: The article was published on April 15, 2026, and has an 11-minute read time.
